# Create static LDAP roles

Configure static roles to map names in Vault to LDAP entries and use the
rotation settings to manage credentials automatically with the role.

<Tip title="Assumptions">

- You have [set up an `ldap` plugin](/vault/docs/secrets/ldap/setup). 
- You have permission to update roles in Vault.
- You have permission to make `POST` calls to the `ldap` plugin.

</Tip>

For self-managed roles, use Vault Enterprise 2.2.0 or later and set
`self_managed=true` when you first configure the mount with the CLI or API.
You cannot change the management setting after configuration, and the GUI
configuration form does not include it. Do not set `bindpass` on a self-managed
mount.

For example, if you enable a new LDAP plugin at the path `self-managed-ldap`:

```shell-session
$ vault secrets enable -path=self-managed-ldap ldap
```

You can then configure self-management for the plugin using `vault write`:

```shell-session
$ vault write self-managed-ldap/config \
    url="ldaps://ldap.example.com" \
    schema="openldap" \
    self_managed=true
```

<Tabs>

<Tab heading="CLI" group="cli">

1. Create a configuration file, `ldap-role.json`, with your role settings:

   @include 'ldap/example-config/static-role/basic.mdx'

   You must set `password` to the current account password for a self-managed mount.

1. Save the new role:

   @include 'ldap/create-static-role/cli.mdx'

   For example, to create a self-managed role without a configuration file:

   ```shell-session
   $ vault write self-managed-ldap/static-role/billing-svc \
       dn="cn=billing-svc,ou=services,dc=example,dc=com" \
       username="billing-svc" \
       password="<current-password>" \
       rotation_period=0
   ```

1. Confirm the role settings by requesting credentials from the plugin:

   @include 'ldap/get-role-creds/cli.mdx'

</Tab>

<Tab heading="API" group="api">

1. Create a configuration file, `ldap-role.json`, with your role settings:

   @include 'ldap/example-config/static-role/basic.mdx'

   You must set `password` to the current account password for a self-managed mount.

1. Save the new role:

   @include 'ldap/create-static-role/api.mdx'

1. Confirm the role settings by requesting credentials from the plugin:

   @include 'ldap/get-role-creds/api.mdx'

</Tab>

<Tab heading="GUI" group="gui">

The GUI reads the `self_managed` setting from the mount configuration and
displays the matching form. Follow the section for your mount type.

Your policy must grant the following capabilities:

| GUI action | Path | Capability |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Detect the mount type | `<mount>/config` | `read` |
| Show **Create role** and create the role | `<mount>/static-role/<name>` | `create` |
| View the role | `<mount>/static-role/<name>` | `read` |
| Show the **Password** row and **Get credentials** | `<mount>/static-cred/<name>` | `read` |

For example:

```hcl
path "<mount>/config"        { capabilities = ["read"] }
path "<mount>/static-role/*" { capabilities = ["create", "read", "list"] }
path "<mount>/static-cred/*" { capabilities = ["read"] }
```

The form covers the role name, distinguished name, username, password, and
rotation period. To set other parameters, such as `password_policy` or
`rotation_schedule`, use the CLI or API.

### Root-managed mount

1. Log into the Vault GUI using a token with the appropriate permissions.
1. Open **Secrets engines** in the navigation.
1. Select your root-managed LDAP mount from the dashboard.
1. Select the **Roles** tab.
1. Click **Create role** to open the creation form.
1. For **Role type**, select **Static role**.
1. Enter a **Role name**, such as `billing-svc`.
1. Enter the **Username** of the account.
1. Optionally, enter the **Distinguished name** of the account, such as:

   `cn=billing-svc,ou=services,dc=example,dc=com`

1. Optionally, enter the current LDAP **Password** of the account. Vault returns
   the password as the starting password until the first rotation.
1. Optionally, set **Rotation period** to the interval between automatic
   password rotations. Leave the field empty or enter `0` to disable automatic
   rotation.
1. Click **Create role**.

Vault creates the role and opens the details page for the role.

### Self-managed mount

Self-managed mounts support only static roles, so the creation form does not
display role type options.

1. Log into the Vault GUI using a token with the appropriate permissions.
1. Open **Secrets engines** in the navigation.
1. Select your self-managed LDAP mount from the dashboard.
1. Select the **Roles** tab.
1. Click **Create role** to open the **Create static role** form.
1. Enter a **Role name**, such as `billing-svc`.
1. Enter the **Distinguished name** of the account, such as:

   `cn=billing-svc,ou=services,dc=example,dc=com`

   You cannot change the distinguished name after you create the role.

1. Enter the **Username** of the account.
1. Enter the current LDAP **Password** of the account. Vault uses the current
   password to manage future rotations.
1. Optionally, set **Rotation period** to the interval between automatic
   password rotations. Leave the field empty or enter `0` to disable automatic
   rotation.
1. Click **Create role**.

Vault creates the role and opens the details page for the role.

### View the role credentials

1. On the details page for the role, click the eye icon in the **Password** row
   to show the password. The GUI reads `<mount>/static-cred/<name>`.
1. Use the copy icon to copy the password value.
1. Click **Get credentials** to open the credentials page.

The credentials page displays the following fields:

| Field | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Last Vault rotation | When Vault last rotated the password, or `Never` if Vault has not rotated it. |
| Password | The current password, masked by default. |
| Username | The LDAP username. |
| Rotation period | The configured rotation period. `0` means automatic rotation is off. |
| Time remaining | The time until the next automatic rotation. |

Depending on your version, Vault displays one of the following values for roles
it has not rotated at least once:

- v2.2.0 and v2.2.1 display a placeholder date in the year 0001.
- v2.2.2 and later display `Never`.

### Restricted permissions

If your policy does not grant `read` on `<mount>/config`, the GUI cannot detect
the mount type. The creation page then displays the warning **Unable to
determine LDAP configuration mode** and the root-managed form.

When you submit the form, Vault applies any rules configured for the mount. On a
self-managed mount, Vault rejects a role without a distinguished name or
password, and the form displays the error. Add the missing value and click
**Create role** again.

To display the self-managed form, grant `read` on `<mount>/config`.
